summary.name: Google SRE book notes
summary.one_liner: A chapter-by-chapter set of personal reading notes on Google's "Site Reliability Engineering" book, written by Dan Luu.
use_cases: Learning SRE practices from Google's book
summary.what_it_does: Dan Luu's handwritten-then-transcribed notes on the book "Site Reliability Engineering" from Google, going chapter by chapter. It summarizes key ideas such as the 50% cap on ops work, error budgets, SLO target setting, eliminating toil, monitoring design (alerts, tickets, logging), Borgmon time-series monitoring, on-call balance, and emergency response. Alongside the summaries, the author adds his own commentary and skepticism about several points. Some chapters are skipped in the notes, and the page says so.
notable: Covers the SRE book chapter by chapter with the author's own commentary in italics
Includes Borgmon monitoring details such as counters vs gauges and time-series storage sizing
Includes worked emergency-response postmortem examples from the book
caveats: Secondary notes on a book, not the book itself; several chapters have no notes
Author states some sections are skipped or left for later re-reading
